summary: A 1955/56 L-4 tower replacing a 1924 D-6 cupola on Granite Mountain near Snoqualmie Pass, volunteer-staffed June-September and reached by a steep 4-mile trail.

facts.design: L-4 tower, 10 ft, replaced a 1924 D-6 cupola cabin

access.note: Reachable by trail; visitors welcome inside during the day when open and volunteer-staffed, but no camping at the lookout and no potable water on site.

visit.trail_note: Granite Mountain Trail 1016 from Pratt Lake trailhead, about 4 miles one way with ~3,500-3,800 ft elevation gain; roughly 8 miles round trip per USFS.

facts.agency: U.S. Forest Service, Mt. Baker-Snoqualmie National Forest (volunteer-staffed via Snoqualmie Fire Lookouts Association)

events.note: A D-6 cupola cabin was erected at the summit, replacing an earlier simple cabin.
Served as an Aircraft Warning Service site during WWII.
NHLR and firelookout.com date the replacement with the current L-4 tower to 1955.
Snoqualmie Fire Lookouts Association dates the upgrade to the present L-4 tower to 1956.
Registered on the National Historic Lookout Register June 9, 2015.

evidence.supports: 1924 D-6 cupola cabin, WWII AWS use, 1956 upgrade to L-4, renovation status, trail distance/elevation, no camping/water
evidence.quote: In 1924 a D-6 cupola cabin was erected at the peak of Granite Mountain where the current lookout resides. After serving as an Aircraft Warning System (AWS) site during WWII, the lookout was upgraded in 1956 to the present 10 foot L-4 tower.

evidence.supports: built 1955, replaced a 1924 lookout, volunteer staffed June-September
evidence.quote: This lookout has provided views of the Cascades since 1955. It replaced a previous 1924 lookout on the same site. It is staffed by volunteers from June through September each year.

evidence.supports: 1920 cabin, 1924 D-6 cupola, present 10-ft L-4 tower built 1955, volunteer care
evidence.quote: Developed about 1920 with a cabin, an elevated D-6 cupola cabin was constructed in 1924. The present 10' treated timber L-4 tower, built in 1955, is presently cared for by volunteers.

evidence.supports: first built 1924, replaced 1955, volunteer staffed June-Sept, visitors welcome day, no camping/picnic tables, elevation 5,600 ft, trail distance
evidence.quote: It was first built in 1924 and replaced in 1955. Volunteers staff and maintain it June through September. Visitors are welcome during the day when the lookout is open.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: NHLR, firelookout.com, and USFS all say the current L-4 tower dates to 1955; the Snoqualmie Fire Lookouts Association says 1956. Both years are reported.

sources.title: Granite Mountain Lookout
sources.publisher: Mount Baker-Snoqualmie National Forest, U.S. Forest Service

notes_for_editor: Access upgraded from 'unknown' to 'public' based on USFS statement that visitors are welcome inside during the day when staffed/open; no camping or potable water at the site. Build-year conflict (1955 vs 1956 for the current tower) resolved by reporting both. Fact-check 2026-10-04: two footnotes in the story misattributed claims that are sourced to [1] (Snoqualmie Fire Lookouts Association) to [2]/[3]/[4] instead -- the 'early-2020s renovation' claim and the 'no camping on the deck' claim both trace only to the SFLA page, not to NHLR or firelookout.com; footnotes corrected.
